function: Learned CSI refinement (Pre-Net MLPs on EM-extracted channel parameters), symbol detection (Rec-Net MLP classifier) and channel-correlation prediction (Correlator-Net transformer) for RIS massive MIMO (pp. 5-9)
system: TDD massive MIMO BS (M antennas) serving K IoT devices via passive reflecting RIS (N elements); 4 GHz mean frequency; M, N, K values not stated (pp. 3, 12)
method: Pre-Net: three MLPs refine EM-extracted channel parameters; Rec-Net: MLP softmax classifier, cross-entropy; Correlator-Net: transformer encoder predicting correlation; offline supervised training (pp. 5-9)
data_channel: Own simulator: LoS BS-RIS and multipath NLOS BS-IoT/RIS-IoT channels with Gaussian gains, AR(1) time variation; 12,000 samples per SNR for Pre-Net, 15,000 symbol pairs for Rec-Net (pp. 3, 6, 8)
test_conditions: Trained per SNR on simulated data; BER over 10,000 random channel realizations per SNR; one system setting (50 km/h, 4 GHz); transferability left to future work (pp. 6, 12-13)
baselines: Non-learned: LS with sampling receiver, imperfect CSI, system without DL. Learned: DnCNN [31], BiLSTM [32], CNN-LSTM [33]; ablations Pre-Net only, Rec-Net only (pp. 12-13)
metrics: BER, MSE of channel parameters, SINR, detection accuracy, correlation prediction error (pp. 8, 12-13)
complexity: Estimator order O(LN log(LN)) + O(It Q) (p. 10); EM part O(Q It) (p. 5); DL module excluded as lightweight, no operation or parameter counts (p. 10)
q1_support: p. 3: "The BS-IoT channel hmk and RIS-IOT channel hnk are both assumed independent and non-line-of-sight (NLOS) and follow the same multipath model, given as [25]"; custom Gaussian-gain simulator with a LoS BS-RIS array-manifold channel; no 3GPP, DeepMIMO, COST 2100 or measured data.
q2_support: p. 6: "trained offline with simulated data at each SNR"; p. 12: "employing 10000 random channel realizations at each SNR" (an SNR sweep). Missing: any test on another scenario, RIS size, band or mobility; p. 13 lists "the transferability of deep learning models across different channel conditions and RIS configurations" as a future challenge.
q3_support: p. 13: "We selected the denoising-based estimation [31], BiLSTM-based estimation and detection framework [32], and CNN-LSTM-based estimation [33] for comparison" (earlier learned methods, BER, Fig. 8); non-learned LS / sampling receiver in Fig. 8 and "a system without such support" in Fig. 9 (p. 13), both on BER.
q4_support: p. 10: "The computational complexity of the proposed channel estimation algorithm is O(LN log(LN)) + O(It Q)"; the DL module is excluded for its "lightweight MLP design", so the order covers the FFT and EM stages only.
q5_support: p. 6: "The DNNs were trained using TensorFlow on datasets comprising 12, 000 noisy indices and corresponding channel gains for each SNR"; the data are the authors' own simulation, and no link, DOI or public dataset is given for code or data.
notes: Area 2 chosen because four of the five networks (three Pre-Net MLPs and Correlator-Net) estimate or predict the channel (Table I, p. 8) and Pre-Net alone gives most of the BER gain (p. 12, Fig. 6); area 1 is possible because BER is the headline metric and the abstract (p. 1) claims detection accuracy, so the reviewer should confirm. The phase shift optimization and the event-triggered pilot control use ADMM and are not learned (pp. 6-11). q4 is met only on the stated order of the estimator, which excludes the DL module as lightweight, so the reviewer should confirm that this counts.
